s: A child born in India between 26 January 1950 and 30 June 1987 acquired citizenship by birth irrespective of the nationality of the parents, subject to the statutory exceptions. Which one of the following is one such exception?
o: A child whose one parent is an Indian citizen
A child born to two Indian citizens
A child whose birth is registered in India
x: Children of foreign diplomats and enemy aliens cannot acquire Indian citizenship by birth. The nationality of the parents was otherwise immaterial during this period.
tq: Use the exception trap in an otherwise broad birth-citizenship rule.
sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to citizenship by birth, consider the following statements:
1. A person born in India from 1 July 1987 to 2 December 2004 could acquire citizenship if at least one parent was an Indian citizen at the time of birth.
2. For a person born in India on or after 3 December 2004, both parents must necessarily be Indian citizens.
3. From 3 December 2004, one Indian-citizen parent is sufficient if the other parent is not an illegal migrant.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because, from 3 December 2004, one parent may be an Indian citizen if the other is not an illegal migrant.
tq: Track the change in the birth rule across the three date ranges.
sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents citizenship by descent under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
o: Born outside India, with either parent being an Indian citizen at the time of birth, and birth registered at an Indian consulate
Born in India and one parent an Indian citizen
Born outside India and resident in India for five years
Born in a territory incorporated into India and notified by the Central Government
x: Citizenship by descent applies to a person born outside India when either parent was an Indian citizen at the time of birth, subject to registration of the birth at an Indian consulate.
tq: Distinguish descent from birth, registration and incorporation by location of birth.

tq: Split the aggregate residence period into its statutory components.

The requirement that the person must be a foreign national
The residence condition for distinguished service to science, art, literature or world peace
The power of the Central Government to grant citizenship

Every person who enters India without registration

A mode available only through incorporation of territory

s:

2. Termination follows automatically when an Indian citizen voluntarily acquires the citizenship of another country.
3. Deprivation can be ordered by the Central Government in specified cases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The three modes of loss are renunciation, automatic termination on voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship, and deprivation by the Central Government in specified cases.
tq: Separate voluntary declaration, automatic consequence and governmental action.

2. Inner Line Permit areas in Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Sixth Schedule tribal areas in the four specified States and Inner Line Permit areas in the four specified States are exempt. All districts of West Bengal are not exempted under this provision.
tq: Identify the two recognised exemption categories and reject an overbroad claim.
sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

s: Under the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026, an approved CAA applicant holding a Pakistani, Afghan or Bangladeshi passport is required to surrender that passport within:
x: The foreign passport must be surrendered within 15 days of approval under the 2026 Rules.
tq: Use a duration-based numerical trap with nearby time periods.
sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

s: The constitutional validity of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 has primarily been challenged with reference to:
x: The challenge principally invokes Article 14, particularly concerning classification based on religion and country.
tq: Match the constitutional challenge with the relevant Article.
sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

s: Who has the exclusive power to make laws regulating citizenship in India?
x: Article 11 empowers Parliament to make laws regarding acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters relating to citizenship.
tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to constitutional powers.
sec: Competent authority to regulate citizenship - article and body

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the roles of the Union Home Ministry and the Election Commission in citizenship matters?
o: The Election Commission alone regulates acquisition and termination of citizenship.
The Home Ministry frames citizenship rules, while the Election Commission checks citizenship for electoral rolls.
The Home Ministry checks electoral rolls, while the Election Commission frames citizenship rules.
Both bodies jointly prescribe all conditions of citizenship.
x: The Union Home Ministry frames citizenship rules, whereas the Election Commission checks citizenship in relation to electoral rolls under Article 324.
tq: Discriminate between two authorities by matching each body with its specific function.
sec: Competent authority to regulate citizenship - article and body

s: The Citizenship Rules, 2009 were framed by the:
x: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs frames the Citizenship Rules, including the Citizenship Rules, 2009.
tq: Use the ministry-function association trap.
sec: Competent authority to regulate citizenship - article and body

s: Which of the following countries follow the principle of dual citizenship at the national and sub-national levels?
o: The United States of America and Switzerland
x: The United States and Switzerland recognise national as well as state or cantonal citizenship. India follows single citizenship.
tq: Use a confusable country-comparison pair.
sec: Single vs dual citizenship - Indian position, other countries, domicile

s: India's system of single citizenship was borrowed chiefly from the constitutional practice of:
x: The Indian Constitution adopted the idea of single citizenship from Britain. Canada also follows single citizenship.
tq: Test the source of a borrowed constitutional feature.
sec: Single vs dual citizenship - Indian position, other countries, domicile

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India provides for one citizenship for the Union and the States.
2. The Constitution recognises a separate constitutional domicile for every State.
3. Article 9 is associated with the prohibition of voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: India has single citizenship and Article 9 deals with voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship. The Constitution does not recognise a separate State domicile in the constitutional sense.
tq: Use one reversed domicile statement to test the single-citizenship concept.
sec: Single vs dual citizenship - Indian position, other countries, domicile

s: Which of the following documents is NOT conclusive proof of Indian citizenship?
o: Certificate of citizenship issued under law
x: Aadhaar is not proof of citizenship. A passport is a travel document and is also not, by itself, conclusive proof of citizenship; voter ID and ration cards are likewise not citizenship proof.
tq: Distinguish identity or travel documents from conclusive citizenship documents.
sec: Single vs dual citizenship - Indian position, other countries, domicile

s: A person who is a foreign citizen of Indian origin, or the spouse or child of such a person, may generally be eligible for:
x: Foreign citizens of Indian origin, their spouses and children may be eligible for an Overseas Citizen of India card, subject to statutory conditions.
tq: Identify the legal status from the eligibility description.
sec: OCI cardholder - eligibility, who is barred, rights not available

s: Which one of the following persons is barred from eligibility for an OCI card?
o: A foreign citizen whose ancestor was an Indian national
A child of an eligible person of Indian origin
A spouse of an eligible person of Indian origin
x: Foreign military personnel are barred from OCI eligibility. Persons connected with Indian origin may otherwise qualify subject to the prescribed conditions.
tq: Find the statutory exclusion among otherwise eligible categories.
sec: OCI cardholder - eligibility, who is barred, rights not available

s:
OCI cardholders are barred from which of the following rights?
1. Voting in elections
2. Contesting elections
3. Holding constitutional offices
4. Public employment as a general rule
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: OCI cardholders are not Indian citizens and do not have voting rights, the right to contest elections, eligibility for constitutional offices or public employment as a general rule.
tq: Use a comprehensive rights-and-disqualifications list.
sec: OCI cardholder - eligibility, who is barred, rights not available

s: Which one of the following statements regarding an OCI cardholder is correct?
o: An OCI cardholder is an Indian citizen with restricted voting rights.
An OCI cardholder is entitled to contest elections but cannot hold public employment.
An OCI cardholder may obtain lifelong visa-free entry, but the OCI card does not confer citizenship.
An OCI cardholder can hold any constitutional office except that of President.
x: An OCI card provides lifelong visa-free entry, but an OCI holder remains a foreign citizen and is not an Indian citizen.
tq: Separate OCI status from Indian citizenship and associated political rights.
sec: OCI cardholder - eligibility, who is barred, rights not available

s: The OCI card alone has been sufficient for lifelong visa-free entry into India since:

2. A central OCI database
3. Online application and renunciation facilities
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The 2026 Rules introduced e-OCI cards, a central OCI database and online application and renunciation facilities.
tq: Treat a set of administrative reforms as a single coded list.
sec: OCI cardholder - eligibility, who is barred, rights not available

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their formation or attainment of the stated status:
A. Andhra State
B. Andhra Pradesh
C. Mizoram as a State
D. Telangana
Select the correct answer.
x: Andhra State was formed in 1953, Andhra Pradesh in 1956, Mizoram became a State in 1987 and Telangana was formed in 2014.

tq: Match the Statehood date with both the statute and amendment.
sec: Formation of states and UTs → year and Act/amendment, chronology

s: Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014 under the:

s:
India may acquire foreign territory through which of the following means?

2. Treaty
3. Conquest

Admit or establish new States not forming part of India
Alter the name of an existing State only

s:
Consider the following statements regarding a Bill under Article 3:

Ordinary laws and are not deemed amendments under Article 368
Subject to approval by every affected State legislature
Amendments under Article 368 requiring a special majority

o: B.R. Ambedkar, K.M. Munshi and H.N. Kunzru
K.M. Panikkar, Jawaharlal Nehru and B.R. Ambedkar
Fazl Ali, Sardar Patel and Rajendra Prasad
Fazl Ali, K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru

s:

The Land Boundary Agreement between India and Bangladesh
The creation of the National Capital Territory of Delhi

s: Under the Land Boundary Agreement with Bangladesh, India transferred and received enclaves in which of the following combinations?

s: At present, the number of Union Territories in India is:

Which of the following Union Territories are represented in the Rajya Sabha?

3. Jammu and Kashmir

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legal status of an Indian passport in determining citizenship?
o: It is conclusive proof of Indian citizenship in every case.
It can be issued only to Indian citizens under the Passports Act, 1967.
It is a travel document and is not conclusive proof of citizenship.
It proves citizenship but not identity.
x: A passport is a travel document and is not conclusive proof of citizenship. Section 20 of the Passports Act, 1967, permits non-citizens to obtain passports in specified circumstances.
tq: Distinguish a travel document from conclusive proof of citizenship and identity.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Aadhaar:
1. Aadhaar establishes identity.
2. Aadhaar is conclusive proof of citizenship.
3. Aadhaar is not, by itself, proof of citizenship under Section 9 of the Aadhaar Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Aadhaar proves identity but not citizenship. Therefore, statements 1 and 3 are correct, while statement 2 is false.
tq: Trap the common confusion between identity proof and citizenship proof.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NPR — persons granted citizenship under the CAA alone
x: The National Register of Citizens concerns citizens only, whereas the National Population Register covers all usual residents. Thus, NRC—citizens only is correctly matched.
tq: Separate the narrower citizenship register from the broader residents’ register.
sec: Universal angles

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The CAA has been challenged under Article 14 because it uses religion and country of origin in deciding eligibility.
2. The debate concerning the CAA includes the relationship between a religion-based test and the equality guarantee under Article 14.
3. The CAA challenge is based exclusively on the constitutional validity of Article 239.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The challenge concerns the use of religion and country of origin in relation to Article 14; Article 239 is unrelated to this issue.
tq: Find the unrelated constitutional provision in a set of closely connected statements.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which one of the following reflects the change in the broad basis of Indian citizenship mentioned in contemporary debates?
o: From territorial citizenship to provincial citizenship
From jus sanguinis to jus soli
From jus soli to jus sanguinis
From single citizenship to dual citizenship
x: India has shifted from jus soli, citizenship based primarily on place of birth, towards jus sanguinis, citizenship based primarily on descent or blood relationship.
tq: Discriminate between the two Latin expressions by their underlying basis of citizenship.
sec: Universal angles

s: In the context of recent administrative developments, citizenship-related work under the CAA was moved to which authority?
x: Citizenship-related work under the CAA was moved to District Collectors. This is an administrative development concerning the processing of citizenship matters.
tq: Identify the authority assigned the function rather than the body that legislated on the subject.
sec: Universal angles

s:
With reference to citizenship verification during electoral roll revision, consider the following statements:
1. The Election Commission of India may check citizenship during roll revision.
2. Doubtful cases may be referred to the Central Government.
3. The Election Commission alone finally determines every doubtful citizenship case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Election Commission may check citizenship during revision of electoral rolls, while doubtful cases may go to the Central Government. It is incorrect to state that the Election Commission alone finally determines every doubtful case.
tq: Distinguish an initial checking role from the authority handling doubtful cases.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Andhra Pradesh’s constitutional and political development?
o: Andhra State — first linguistic State; bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh — 2014
Andhra State — first Union Territory; bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh — 2000
Andhra State — first linguistic State; bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh — 1953
Andhra State — first State formed under Article 239; bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh — 2019
x: Andhra State, formed in 1953, was the first linguistic State. Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated in 2014.
tq: Check both parts of a paired historical statement instead of accepting a partially familiar match.
